key_insight: Instead of ranking samples by their instantaneous loss, AlignPrune scores examples by how their loss evolves over time (loss-trajectory alignment), enabling dynamic pruning that distinguishes true hard examples from noisy-label outliers.
problem_solved: Dynamic data pruning methods that rely on per-sample loss tend to retain noisy-label samples (which often exhibit high loss), degrading model performance under label noise; this work makes pruning robust to such noisy labels.
method: Introduce Dynamic Alignment Score (DAS): a metric that compares a sample's loss trajectory to expected/typical trajectories, downweighting or removing samples whose trajectories indicate label noise rather than genuine difficulty.
Integrate DAS as a lightweight, plug-and-play module into existing dynamic pruning pipelines to guide sample retention/removal decisions over training steps.
Operate on trajectory information (temporal loss patterns) rather than single-step loss values to reduce false preservation of noisy examples.
impact: Practitioners can apply dynamic pruning more safely in noisy-label scenarios, improving model generalization and compression decisions without manually cleaning labels; AlignPrune is a practical plug-in for robust, efficient training.
visual_elements: Line plot comparing loss trajectories: clean example (smooth/decaying) vs noisy-label example (persistently high or erratic) with DAS illustration.
Flowchart of training loop showing standard dynamic pruning vs AlignPrune-enhanced loop (DAS computation -> prune decision).
Bar chart or table showing relative retained noisy samples and validation accuracy with/without AlignPrune under increasing label noise.
Icon set: stopwatch (temporal/trajectory), filter/pruner (pruning), shield (robustness), plug (plug-and-play module).
paper_title: Beyond Loss Values: Robust Dynamic Pruning via Loss Trajectory Alignment
paper_authors: Huaiyuan Qin, Muli Yang, Gabriel James Goenawan, Kai Wang, Zheng Wang
